newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-Suzutan officials accused of insider trading.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Suzutan officials accused of insider trading.

text.p: Japan's securities watchdog filed accusations of insider trading on Tuesday against three former Suzutan Co officials and a former official of a subsidiary to prosecutors in Nagoya, central Japan, government sources said.

The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission filed the accusations on grounds that the officials had sold Suzutan shares before disclosing that a subsidiary was likely to post appraisal losses of 2.1 billion yen and that there was a possibility that Suzutan had unpayable, guaranteed debts totalling 3.0 billion yen, the sources said.

Katsurao Suzui, one of the officials accused, resigned from the post of president at the women's apparel retailing firm in March. He earlier acknowledged that he sold 1.01 million shares in the company prior to an announcement of a loss for the 1994/95 business year, but said he did not regard this as improper.
